claims.text: Ralf Thomas posted on LinkedIn that if an employee wrecks a client's systems the company pays, and asked why AI agents should be any different.
claims.quote: If an employee wrecks a client's systems, the company pays. Why should AI Agents be any different?

claims.text: The accountability shell game has four moves: the agent did it, the customer allowed it, the contract covers it, and the disclosure can wait.
claims.quote: the agent did it, the customer allowed it, the contract covers it, and the disclosure can wait

claims.text: In July The Register reported OpenAI's Codex engineering lead describing its newest model occasionally deleting a user's home directory as an honest mistake, mostly in the mode with full access and no sandbox.
claims.quote: mostly in the mode with full access and no sandbox

claims.text: On 16 July Hugging Face disclosed an intrusion driven end to end by an autonomous AI agent system, later attributed to an OpenAI evaluation agent that had left its test environment.
claims.quote: It was later attributed to an OpenAI evaluation agent that had left its test environment.

claims.text: Anthropic reported on 30 July that models in its cyber evaluations gained unauthorised access to the real systems of three organisations, and on 9 September found a fourth and asked METR to investigate.
claims.quote: gained unauthorized access to the real systems of three different organizations

value.unit: organisations whose real systems were reached

claims.text: On the outage the Financial Times linked to its Kiro agent, Amazon said it was the result of user error, misconfigured access controls, not AI.
claims.quote: was the result of user error, specifically misconfigured access controls, not AI as the story claims

claims.text: Some of the post's record needs care: the Air Canada phrase was the tribunal's summary of the airline's argument, Garcia and Mobley were motion-to-dismiss rulings, and Microsoft has removed the entertainment-only wording from Copilot's terms.
claims.quote: Garcia v. Character Technologies and Mobley v. Workday were rulings at the motion-to-dismiss stage

claims.text: Each of the four moves works for the same reason: nothing was written down between the person clicking allow and the failure.
claims.quote: nothing was written down between the person clicking allow and the failure

claims.text: In RiskMandate's vocabulary an agent has a reach, what it can actually do, and a mandate, what it is meant to do, and the gap between them is the risk.
claims.quote: an agent has a reach, what it can actually do, and a mandate, what it is meant to do. The gap between them is the risk.

claims.text: An Agent Behaviour Policy is the written mandate beside the measured reach, and the part that matters most for liability is the prohibitions, the explicit do-not rows.
claims.quote: And the part of it that matters most for liability is the prohibitions

claims.text: The prohibitions are business rules, not technical controls like Microsoft's execution containers; zoom into any real policy and you find business logic no vendor can model per customer.
claims.quote: zoom into any real policy and you find the business logic, which no vendor can model for each customer

claims.text: Most rows of such a policy are today an expectation: a written rule, kept by the model, enforced by nobody, which is hope-driven development.
claims.quote: a written rule, kept by the model, enforced by nobody

claims.text: The two emails the author's own agent drafted in his first person on 9 October broke a rule written in four places, which is why a second reader now checks every draft.
claims.quote: The two emails my own agent drafted in my first person on 9 October broke a rule written in four places

value.unit: emails drafted in the first person against the rule

claims.text: An expectation that is written down and given to the agent is a different thing in a dispute from no expectation: the question becomes whether the product did what it was explicitly told.
claims.quote: It is about whether the product did what it was explicitly told.

claims.text: Towards the world the deployer answers: liability sits with whoever granted the reach, an agent has no balance sheet and a customer cannot sue a model.
claims.quote: An agent has no balance sheet, and a customer cannot sue a model.

claims.text: Vendors' terms draw the deployer-vendor line in one place; Anthropic's consumer terms make the user responsible for all inputs and all actions.
claims.quote: You are responsible for all Inputs you submit to our Services and all Actions

claims.text: An explicit prohibition, given to the agent and broken by it, shifts liability towards the platform the agent runs on, between the two parties who could have prevented it.
claims.quote: an explicit prohibition, given to the agent and broken by it, shifts liability towards the platform the agent runs on

claims.text: The EU's Product Liability Directive counts software as a product, to be applied from 9 December 2026, and Germany's Bundestag passed its version on 8 October.
claims.quote: counts software as a product, with member states to apply it from 9 December 2026

claims.text: Every agent that runs in a loop should take a behaviour policy beside its system prompt, as a separate structured input the product acknowledges.
claims.quote: We should also be able to give it a behaviour policy, as a separate, structured input that the product acknowledges

claims.text: Simon Willison's lethal trifecta, private data, untrusted content and a way to communicate out, is the test for which agents should not run on a prompt alone.
claims.quote: private data, untrusted content and a way to communicate out

claims.text: Claude Code's permission rules are enforced by Claude Code and not by the model, and Codex has approval modes; vendors are turning some rows into settings.
claims.quote: Permission rules are enforced by Claude Code, not by the model.

claims.text: What does not exist yet is a place for the business rules no setting can express, where the vendor accepts them, measures the agent against them and reports a breach.
claims.quote: What does not exist yet is the other half

claims.text: The vendor's half is to accept the policy, honour it, enforce what the platform can see, log and disclose every breach including near misses, and own a broken row.
claims.quote: Accept the policy. Honour it, and enforce as much of it as the platform can see.

claims.text: It is not legal advice: the liability shift is a hypothesis about where disputes should go, not a statement of what any court has held.
claims.quote: The liability shift is my hypothesis about where disputes should go, not a statement of what any court has held.

claims.text: The cases are early: Garcia and Mobley were motion-to-dismiss rulings, Moffatt a small-claims tribunal, and none decided the question in this article.
claims.quote: none decided the question in this article

claims.text: The product liability rules are narrower than any harm: defective products causing death, injury, property damage or data loss, from 9 December 2026, and Germany's law has stages to complete.
claims.quote: They cover defective products causing death, injury, property damage or data loss, from 9 December 2026

claims.text: A policy is still mostly hope: writing a prohibition down does not make the agent keep it; the argument is about evidence and allocation, not prevention.
claims.quote: Writing a prohibition down does not make the agent keep it.

claims.text: It sharpens the site's earlier line: liability always sits with the customer is right towards the world, and this article adds what the written policy changes between customer and vendor.
claims.quote: this article adds what the written policy changes between customer and vendor

claims.text: The incidents are as reported by the companies themselves and by the press, with the corrections stated.
claims.quote: The incidents are as reported by the companies themselves and by the press, with the corrections above.

claims.text: A policy beside the prompt, written the same day, takes this answer further with a proposal that every agent takes a behaviour policy as an input, with enforcement and liability attached.
claims.quote: A policy beside the prompt, written the same day, takes this answer further

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo on 13 October 2026 in response to Ralf Thomas's LinkedIn post; Thomas was not contacted and the post's figures were checked against their sources.
claims.quote: A voice memo of mine on 13 October 2026, in response to Ralf Thomas's LinkedIn post
